glossary.definition: After user consent, RFC 8693 token exchange mints a delegated token: sub is the USER, act={sub: agent} names the actor. Every action traces back to a real human — a chain of custody, not guesswork.

The policy reads directory groups on EVERY decision: a user outside the required group is denied regardless of scopes, and the premium group EXPANDS capability (restricted tools + a higher amount ceiling). Promotion is instant — no code change, no redeploy.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol: tools/call
sources.use: The JSON-RPC tool-call shape the transfer gate scopes.

cards.label: Scenario 1: UC1: consent mints act={agent}, the balance read permits
cards.description: The user consented; the delegated token carries sub=user, act={agent}. The chain validates and the entitled read permits — fully attributable.

cards.label: Scenario 2: ROGUE ACTOR: an unknown agent is refused at the gateway
cards.description: The actor allow-list: act.sub must name a registered agent. An unauthorized actor is refused before the policy is even consulted (the app fixed this check being dead code).

cards.label: Scenario 3: UC9: not in the required group — denied regardless of scopes
cards.description: The group gate fires first: a user outside the required group is denied no matter what the token carries. The directory groups are read on every decision.

cards.label: Scenario 4: UC9A: flip the directory entry, the very next call moves
cards.description: Live directory: the first call denies; flip the directory entry; the identical call now permits — no code change, no cache, no re-login.

cards.label: Scenario 5: UC21: Standard tier cannot invoke the premium wire
cards.description: Positive least privilege: the premium-only tool is denied for a non-Premium user with a distinct reason — the agent of a Standard user is not even offered it.

cards.label: Scenario 6: UC21: promote to Premium — the same call now permits
cards.description: Directory-driven tiers: adding the premiumTier group instantly expands the tool set and raises the ceiling to $50000. Policy-driven, not hard-coded.

cards.label: Scenario 7: UC21: $60000 exceeds even the Premium ceiling
cards.description: The tier ceiling applies to Premium too: $60000 exceeds $50000 and is denied with tier_amount_exceeded — capability expanded, still bounded.

cards.label: Reconfigure the policy live
cards.description: Change the amount bands live; the SAME call flips on the next run — a crossing edit falls back to the defaults, never wider.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
